notes: SMALLEST HONEST CHANGE. Exists: a policy catalog of 13 domains and 127 issues shipped today; `introduceMeasure` accepting the alternatives a bill chooses between; and a consumer at `legislation-integrity.ts:142` already reading them. Both ends are built. Missing link: none of the seven callers passes the field, so every bill carries an empty list. Smallest honest change: pass it from the one caller a player actually goes through when filing a bill, rather than all seven at once, and leave the institution-generated routes alone until the rule for them is decided. What a player would then see: a bill that is about something — a measure filed against a named issue from the catalog, instead of a measure about nothing while the catalog sits unreachable beside it.

PLAYER-FACING INPUT: filing a bill is reachable — a player does press something. What they cannot do is say what the bill is about, because no filing route passes policyAlternativeIds. The control exists and the field behind it is never filled.
Handed over by the 'What passing a law actually does' lane, which found it outside its own scope, and re-measured here before filing. Their count was six callers; it is seven.

This is a wiring gap rather than a content gap, and it is the same shape the catalog itself had: the vocabulary landed and the thing that would reach it was never called. Worth answering together with the policy domain list rather than after it.
One of four records from this sweep. The others are mod-api-vocabulary-is-two-fields, finished-rooms-waiting-on-a-location and decision-thresholds-are-constants-in-code.
question: When a measure is introduced, which policy alternatives should it carry, and which of the seven paths that introduce measures decides them — the sponsor's own position, the issue the bill is filed under, the body's docket, or the player's choice at the moment of filing?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It establishes that the field exists, is optional, defaults to an empty array and is stored on the measure. It says nothing about who should populate it.

sourcesChecked.source: Every call site of introduceMeasure outside its own module
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It settles the fact and not the intent. Seven callers — legislation-docket.ts:951, legislation-world.ts:434, tax-work.ts:47, legislation-bundle-docket.ts:343, municipal-public-work.ts:1673, legislation-scenarios.ts:732 and governing/legislative-clock.ts:706 — and none passes policyAlternativeIds. Outside the module the field appears only in two test files, each passing an empty array explicitly.
It reads measure.policyAlternativeIds, so there is a consumer waiting and the shape is not vestigial. It does not say what a correct list looks like.

title: What a bill should be about, and where its alternatives come from
usableAnswer: A rule for where the alternatives come from, and whether it is the same rule for all seven paths or differs between a player filing a bill, a scenario seeding one, and the institution generating one. If a bill may legitimately have no alternatives — a purely procedural measure, say — say so, because then the empty list is correct for some callers and the question becomes which ones.
whyItMatters: The policy catalog landed on 2026-09-22 with 13 domains and 127 issues, so the game now knows what politics is about. introduceMeasure accepts the list of alternatives a bill is choosing between, and not one of the seven callers passes it, so every bill in every game carries an empty list. A bill is not about anything. This is the connection between the catalog and the thing a legislator actually does, and until it is made, the catalog is reachable by nothing.
